passages.text: Peter said, ‘Since, then, you are now eager to learn about our worship, I owe you an orderly account, beginning with God himself and showing that he alone must be called God, and that no others should be called or considered gods. Whoever acts otherwise must be punished eternally, as one who has committed the greatest impiety against the very Master of all.’ After saying this, he laid his hands on those troubled by afflictions, the sick, and those possessed by demons, prayed, healed them, and dismissed the crowds. Then he went inside, partook of his customary salt, and slept.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτὸν μόνον δεῖ λέγειν θεόν, ἑτέρους δὲ μήτε λέγειν μήτε νομίζειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: he alone must be called God, and ... no others should be called or considered gods
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both naming and regarding others as gods are prohibited. The rendering does not narrow the claim merely to verbal forms of address.

The plural salt expression may function as a reference to simple customary fare or a shared table. The main text keeps the expressed salt rather than supplying bread or a detailed meal not named here; customary fare is a smoother metonymic alternative.
